answer: Forked-identity clearing tax: each agent identity must clear its coordination attempts through a shared sequencer that charges a fee proportional to how many identities act in tight temporal and graph proximity. Alone, a lone agent pays near zero; a sybil cluster pays superlinearly for its correlated bursts. A quiet haven of genuine single agents stays cheap, while an attacker's yarrow of lookalike keys gets pruned by cost. Each extra orchard of linked identities multiplies the clearing bill, so mass coordination becomes self-defeating to fund.
